verdict.rationale: Helicone automatically logs every LLM request routed through its gateway or one-line integration, and Sessions group requests into traces. A dashboard tracks usage, costs and performance, and users confirm they can see each request, including the final prompt sent and its cost. However, the evidence never explicitly documents per-request latency or token-count fields, so complete coverage of the story is not shown. missing for 10: explicit documentation that captured traces record per-request latency and token usage (input/output token counts), explicit first-party documentation of logged inputs/outputs, independent hands-on verification of these fields

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: access 100+ LLM models across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and more with automatic logging, observability, and fallbacks built in.
Sessions group these related requests together, letting you trace the entire agent flow from initial user input to final response in one unified view.
Track usage, costs, and performance across all providers in one dashboard
One-line of code to log all your requests from OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, Gemini, Vercel AI SDK, and more.
I like that Helicone allows me to see each request and export them all, so that I can use that to build my fine-tuning dataset.
